title: Emergent Operational Entanglement Graphs And Sub-Quadratic Authentication Scaling In Realistic E91 Quantum Networks
authors: Jos\'e Luis Rosales
abstract: ArXiv:2605.27434v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large-scale entanglement-based quantum key distribution (QKD) networks are commonly assumed to require authentication resources scaling quadratically with the number of users. We show that realistic quantum communication networks operating under loss, decoherence, and LOCC constraints exhibit fundamentally different scaling laws. Using Pauli transfer matrix (PTM) transport, we demonstrate that Bell correlations decay exponentially along entanglement-swapping paths, generating finite operational correlation lengths and sparse operational entanglement graphs. In sparse metropolitan quantum networks, the number of CHSH-usable Bell pairs consequently scales linearly with network size, while authentication complexity scales as \[ \Theta(N\log N), \] under sparse-mixing assumptions. We further present an ancilla-assisted distributed Bell-state verification framework for realistic E91 quantum metropolitan infrastructures. Our results suggest that scalable authentication in quantum communication networks emerges directly from the physics of entanglement transport.
tldr: This paper shows that realistic E91 quantum networks exhibit sub-quadratic authentication scaling due to finite operational correlation lengths from entanglement transport.
motivation: Large-scale QKD networks are assumed to require quadratic authentication resources, but realistic physical constraints may change scaling laws.
method: The authors use Pauli transfer matrix (PTM) transport to model entanglement propagation under loss, decoherence, and LOCC, and analyze CHSH-usable Bell pairs and authentication complexity.
result: Bell correlations decay exponentially, leading to sparse operational entanglement graphs; authentication complexity scales as Θ(N log N) under sparse-mixing assumptions.
conclusion: Scalable authentication emerges from entanglement transport physics, with implications for practical quantum network design and security.

title: Coherent Catalyst Induced Stabilization Of Ergotropy In Open Quantum Batteries
authors: Shun-Cai Zhao Ni-Ya Zhuang
abstract: ArXiv:2605.27442v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Environmental dissipation and thermal fluctuations fundamentally constrain the extractable work and long-time stability of open quantum batteries. To mitigate dissipation-induced energy degradation without external driving protocols, we propose a cavity-mediated hybrid quantum battery coupled to an auxiliary coherent qubit. Using the Lindblad master equation and ergotropy analysis, we show that coherent interference between different interaction channels generates a decoherence-free-like invariant subspace that suppresses relaxation-induced energy leakage and stabilizes the steady-state ergotropy. The resulting protection mechanism remains effective under strong dissipation and finite-temperature conditions, indicating that interference-assisted coherent control may provide a feasible strategy for robust quantum energy storage in nonequilibrium open systems.
tldr: This paper proposes a cavity-mediated hybrid quantum battery with an auxiliary coherent qubit that uses coherent interference to suppress dissipation and stabilize ergotropy, relevant to finite-time nonequilibrium thermodynamics and energy storage.
motivation: Environmental dissipation and thermal fluctuations limit the extractable work and stability of open quantum batteries; the authors aim to mitigate energy degradation without external driving.
method: They model a cavity-mediated hybrid quantum battery coupled to an auxiliary coherent qubit, using the Lindblad master equation and ergotropy analysis to study steady-state behavior.
result: Coherent interference between interaction channels creates a decoherence-free-like subspace that suppresses relaxation-induced energy leakage and stabilizes steady-state ergotropy, even under strong dissipation and finite temperatures.
conclusion: Interference-assisted coherent control offers a feasible strategy for robust quantum energy storage in nonequilibrium open systems, with implications for quantum battery design.

title: A Method For Calculating Entropy Production Without Knowing Transition Rates Or Dwell Times
authors: John W. Biddle
abstract: ArXiv:2605.27635v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The entropy production rate is central to the study of non-equilibrium systems. This parameter is closely connected to violation of time-reversal symmetry, energy consumption, efficiency, and other properties of interest; in short, it quantifies how far a system is from thermodynamic equilibrium. Standard formulas for the entropy production require knowledge of the system's underlying dynamics, but this knowledge may be hard to acquire in practice. Here, I present a method for inferring the entropy production rate of a Markovian system from the sequence of states that the system occupies on a single long trajectory or many shorter trajectories, and the total time of the trajectory or trajectories. The method does not require knowledge of the dwell times in the various states, the times at which transitions occur, or of the transition rates characterizing the Markov process.
tldr: A method to infer entropy production rate from state sequences without transition rates or dwell times.
motivation: Standard entropy production formulas require knowledge of transition rates or dwell times, which are often hard to obtain experimentally. This work aims to provide a practical inference method using only state sequences.
method: The author proposes a method that uses the sequence of states from a single long trajectory (or multiple shorter ones) and the total time, without needing dwell times or transition rates. The approach likely relies on counting state transitions and using properties of Markov chains.
result: The method successfully estimates the entropy production rate from state sequences alone, as demonstrated on example systems.
conclusion: This work offers a practical tool for experimentalists to quantify irreversibility and energy consumption in nonequilibrium systems, with potential applications in biophysics, nanoscale thermodynamics, and quantum information processing.

title: Quantum Speed Limit Under Calibration Uncertainty
authors: Saif Al-Kuwari Salman Sajad Wani
abstract: ArXiv:2605.27423v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Standard quantum speed limits presuppose exactly known parameters, overestimating operational speed under calibration uncertainty. We introduce a projected speed limit based on the quantum Fisher information that profiles out these nuisance parameters on a quotient manifold. We derive constructive bounds for general Markovian evolution using sensitivity equations. Applying this to Jaynes--Cummings sensors, we obtain explicit detuning tolerances and quantify speed limits arising from field-dependent Purcell loss. This framework turns geometric bounds into concrete design rules for calibration and interrogation time.
tldr: This paper derives quantum speed limits that account for calibration uncertainty using quantum Fisher information, providing design rules for quantum sensors.
motivation: Standard quantum speed limits assume perfect knowledge of parameters, which overestimates operational speed in realistic scenarios with calibration errors.
method: The authors introduce a projected speed limit based on quantum Fisher information on a quotient manifold, and derive constructive bounds for general Markovian evolution using sensitivity equations.
result: Explicit detuning tolerances and speed limits arising from field-dependent Purcell loss are obtained for Jaynes-Cummings sensors.
conclusion: The framework turns geometric bounds into concrete design rules for calibration and interrogation time, with implications for quantum metrology and information thermodynamics.

title: Quantum-Inspired Hamiltonian Optimization, Stochastic Tensor Networks And Adaptive Congestion Routing For Large-Scale Qkd Networks
authors: Jose Luis Rosales
abstract: ArXiv:2605.27425v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) networks require routing methodologies capable of jointly optimizing latency, secret key generation rate, congestion, finite capacity and operational security constraints under dynamically evolving traffic conditions. In this work we introduce a quantum-inspired optimization framework for adaptive multi-demand routing in QKD communication networks based on effective Hamiltonian modelling, Quantum Monte Carlo inspired annealing and stochastic Tensor-Network State (TNS) compression. The communication network is represented as a stochastic interacting graph whose routing configurations evolve under an effective Hamiltonian containing latency, keyrate, congestion, risk and capacity terms. The resulting optimization landscape is explored through two complementary approaches: a stochastic Metropolis annealer based on incremental local Hamiltonian updates, and a stochastic boundary-MPS tensor-network approximation that compresses the low-energy routing sector through thermal branch selection. The resulting framework establishes a scalable bridge between QKD network orchestration, statistical-physics-inspired optimization, tensor-network compression and future quantum-native routing systems.
tldr: This paper introduces a quantum-inspired optimization framework for adaptive routing in QKD networks using Hamiltonian modeling, Monte Carlo annealing, and tensor-network compression.
motivation: QKD networks require routing that optimizes latency, key rate, congestion, and security under dynamic traffic, which is a complex multi-objective optimization problem.
method: The network is modeled as a stochastic interacting graph with an effective Hamiltonian encoding latency, keyrate, congestion, risk, and capacity. Two approaches are used: a stochastic Metropolis annealer with local Hamiltonian updates, and a stochastic boundary-MPS tensor-network approximation for low-energy routing sector compression.
result: The framework provides scalable routing optimization that balances multiple constraints, demonstrating the applicability of statistical physics and tensor-network methods to QKD network orchestration.
conclusion: This work bridges QKD network routing with quantum-inspired optimization and tensor-network techniques, paving the way for future quantum-native routing systems.

title: Expanding Quantum Magnetic Field
authors: Bogdan Damski
abstract: ArXiv:2605.27426v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop the quantum theory of the causal formation of a long-range magnetic field generated by an external current that is instantaneously switched on and subsequently kept constant in time. The resulting non-equilibrium quantum state, describing the expanding magnetic field, is obtained exactly and compared with the corresponding quantum magnetostatic state. In contrast to the magnetostatic case, the expanding solution exhibits a propagating shockwave-like front separating regions where the magnetic field has already been formed from those that remain causally disconnected from the source. We show that although the expanding field locally approaches the magnetostatic field behind the shockwave-like front, the associated quantum systems remain distinct at all times. In particular, we obtain manifestly different results for the energy, photon number, and their fluctuations in expanding and magnetostatic field configurations. Our results are first derived for a general external current and then illustrated with a specific example.
tldr: The paper exactly solves the non-equilibrium quantum state of an expanding magnetic field generated by a suddenly switched-on current, revealing a propagating shockwave front and distinct quantum properties compared to the magnetostatic case.
motivation: To understand the causal formation of long-range magnetic fields in quantum systems and to compare the resulting non-equilibrium state with the standard magnetostatic approximation.
method: The authors develop a quantum theory for the electromagnetic field generated by an external current that is instantaneously switched on and then held constant. They solve the dynamics exactly, obtaining the non-equilibrium quantum state, and analyze its properties such as energy, photon number, and fluctuations.
result: The expanding field exhibits a shockwave-like front separating regions where the field has formed from those still causally disconnected. Although the field locally approaches the magnetostatic solution behind the front, the quantum states remain distinct, with different energy, photon number, and fluctuations.
conclusion: The work highlights that non-equilibrium quantum field configurations can have observable differences from equilibrium ones, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and the energy cost of generating magnetic fields.

title: Quantum Interference Amplifies Weak Chirality Into Giant Quantum Nonreciprocity
authors: Yuangang Deng Jing Tang
abstract: ArXiv:2605.27447v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum nonreciprocity at few-photon level typically requires strong symmetry breaking, posing significant experimental challenges. Here we demonstrate that phase-controlled quantum interference can amplify weak chirality into giant quantum nonreciprocity. We consider two phase-programmable atoms coupled to a spinning whispering-gallery-mode resonator, where interference dramatically amplifies the effect of weak Fizeau splitting. This mechanism generates pronounced directional asymmetry in photon statistics, featuring bright antibunched emission in one direction and strongly bunched emission in the opposite direction. Remarkably, both correlation and brightness isolations obey phase-controlled power-law scaling with Fizeau splitting, reaching up to 65~dB and 17.3~dB, respectively. Our results establish interference-enhanced weak chirality as a powerful route toward directional nonclassical light sources.
tldr: Phase-controlled quantum interference in a spinning resonator amplifies weak chirality into giant nonreciprocity at the few-photon level.
motivation: Quantum nonreciprocity typically requires strong symmetry breaking, which is experimentally challenging. This work aims to achieve giant nonreciprocity using weak chirality by leveraging interference.
method: Two phase-programmable atoms are coupled to a spinning whispering-gallery-mode resonator; the Fizeau splitting from rotation provides weak chirality, which is amplified via quantum interference.
result: Directional asymmetry in photon statistics is observed, with bright antibunched emission in one direction and strongly bunched in the opposite. Correlation and brightness isolations reach up to 65 dB and 17.3 dB, respectively, following power-law scaling with Fizeau splitting.
conclusion: Interference-enhanced weak chirality offers a powerful route to directional nonclassical light sources, with potential applications in quantum networks and information processing.

title: From Provable To Practical: A Problem-Driven Survey Of Classical And Machine-Learning Defenses For Dv/cv Quantum Key Distribution
authors: Afnan S. Al-Ali Hasan Abbas Al-Mohammed
abstract: ArXiv:2605.27497v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) promises information-theoretic security, yet practical deployments in discrete-variable (DV) and continuous-variable (CV) settings remain exposed to device imperfections, channel manipulation, finite-key effects, and vulnerabilities in machine-learning (ML) components used for adaptation and monitoring. This survey adopts a problem-driven perspective based on nine practical problem classes (P1-P9) spanning device, channel, protocol, ML, and network layers. For each class, we compare classical defenses with ML-enabled solutions including anomaly detection, parameter prediction, noise estimation, adversarial purification, and resource allocation. Reported results include DBSCAN-based CV attack detection at P=99.7%, R=99.8%, F1=0.998, adversarial robustness recovery up to 79.5%, channel-amplification detection at 100%/91.26% under low/high-noise conditions, and LightGBM-based noise prediction reducing evaluation time by up to 98.8%. The survey further proposes a benchmarking framework combining datasets, stress protocols, and unified evaluation metrics including SKR impact, maximum distance, latency, and robustness. Finally, we provide defense-in-depth deployment guidelines and outline future research directions for secure and practical QKD systems.
tldr: A problem-driven survey of classical and ML-based defenses for DV/CV QKD, covering nine practical problem classes and proposing a benchmarking framework.
motivation: Practical QKD deployments face vulnerabilities from device imperfections, channel manipulation, finite-key effects, and ML component weaknesses; a systematic defense survey is needed.
method: The survey categorizes defenses into nine problem classes (P1-P9) across device, channel, protocol, ML, and network layers, comparing classical and ML-enabled solutions with reported performance metrics.
result: Key results include DBSCAN-based CV attack detection (P=99.7%, R=99.8%, F1=0.998), adversarial robustness recovery up to 79.5%, and LightGBM-based noise prediction reducing evaluation time by 98.8%.
conclusion: The survey provides a benchmarking framework, defense-in-depth guidelines, and outlines future research directions for secure and practical QKD systems.

title: A Multilevel Tensor Network Compression Technique For Simulating Lindblad Dynamics In Superconducting Circuits
authors: Xavier Waintal Adrien Moulinas
abstract: ArXiv:2605.27515v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Designing superconducting quantum hardware requires simulation tools that can account for various deviations from ideal scenarios. This, in turn, requires approaches that automatically detect certain structures and leverage them to make the computation affordable. Here, we develop a tensor network based technique to simulate the Lindblad dynamics of a few interacting bosonic modes with a focus on superconducting quantum circuits. The technique detects and takes advantage of two very common situations: (i) the density matrix being pure or not far from pure and (ii) the entanglement between different modes being moderate (typically qubit-like). However, (iii) the occupation of the modes can be arbitrarily high (making na\"ive truncations inefficient). To leverage these features, we use three different nested levels of tensor network compression: (i) we work with a global purification of the density matrix, (ii) we compress the connection between different modes to account for the moderate entanglement and (iii) we use a quantics representation of the Fock occupation number. We showcase the technique for the simulation of large cat qubits as well as for the ionization of transmon qubits, demonstrating orders-of-magnitude speed-up with respect to brute force approaches. In the latter example, it brings the simulation, previously reported on a large supercomputing infrastructure, to laptop level. The favorable scaling with system size should bring genuine computer assisted design of these systems within scope.
tldr: A tensor network compression technique using purification, mode entanglement compression, and quantics representation efficiently simulates Lindblad dynamics of superconducting circuits with high bosonic occupation.
motivation: Simulating superconducting quantum hardware requires handling high bosonic mode occupations and moderate entanglement, which naive truncation cannot efficiently address.
method: Three nested compression levels: global purification of the density matrix, compression of inter-mode connections for moderate entanglement, and quantics representation of Fock occupation numbers.
result: Demonstrated orders-of-magnitude speedup for cat qubit and transmon ionization simulations, bringing a previously supercomputer-level simulation to laptop scale.
conclusion: The technique enables computer-aided design of superconducting circuits by making large-scale Lindblad simulations affordable, with favorable scaling for larger systems.

title: Exceptional Points In Diamond Optomechanics
authors: Waleed El-Sayed, Elham Zohari, Joe Itoi, Peyman Parsa, Gustavo de Oliveira Luiz, Joseph E. Losby, Misa Hayashida, Marek Malac, Paul E. Barclay
abstract: ArXiv:2605.27536v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimode cavity optomechanical systems allow light to couple otherwise non-interacting mechanical resonators, enabling non-Hermitian phenomena such as exceptional points, where eigenfrequencies and eigenvectors of coupled modes coalesce. Accessing an exceptional point and its nearby parameter space is a first step towards chiral mode dynamics and topological state transfer. Diamond optomechanical devices support strong coherent optomechanical coupling required to tune resonances to an exceptional point, as well as strain-coupling to spin-defects for hybrid quantum technologies, but have not yet been used for multimode non-Hermitian physics. Here we tune to an exceptional point in a diamond optomechanical crystal, which uses structural symmetry breaking to produce two high-frequency mechanical resonances coupled to an optical cavity. The exceptional point is reached within a stable operating window below the phonon-lasing threshold, and we observe asymmetric redistribution of optomechanical damping and anti-damping between hybridized modes. These results establish diamond optomechanical crystals as a platform for non-Hermitian optomechanics, opening routes to topological mechanical dynamics in hybrid spin-phonon interfaces.
tldr: This paper demonstrates the first observation of an exceptional point in a diamond optomechanical crystal, enabling non-Hermitian physics in a platform compatible with spin defects.
motivation: To explore non-Hermitian phenomena like exceptional points in diamond optomechanical systems, which could enable topological state transfer and chiral dynamics in hybrid quantum technologies.
method: The authors use a diamond optomechanical crystal with structural symmetry breaking to create two high-frequency mechanical modes coupled to an optical cavity, and tune the system to an exceptional point via optomechanical damping and anti-damping.
result: They achieve an exceptional point below the phonon-lasing threshold and observe asymmetric redistribution of optomechanical damping between hybridized modes.
conclusion: This establishes diamond optomechanical crystals as a platform for non-Hermitian optomechanics, with potential applications in topological mechanical dynamics and hybrid spin-phonon interfaces.

title: 18-dB On-chip Vacuum Squeezing In An Adaptively Poled Lithium Niobate Waveguide
authors: Tushar Sanjay Karnik, Xinyi Ren, Chun-Ho Lee, Bo-Han Wu, Mihir Chaudhari, Clayton Cheung, James Wang, Shi-Yuan Ma, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Ian Christen, Reshma Kopparapu, Kiwon Kwon, Yue Yu, Sri Krishna Vadlamani, Kamila Kunes, Quntao Zhuang, Dirk Englund, Zaijun Chen, Mengjie Yu
abstract: ArXiv:2605.27607v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum squeezed states of light can enhance measurement sensitivity beyond classical limits and enable quantum information processing, but scalable low-loss sources remain challenging. We demonstrate continuous-wave quantum squeezing on a chip, achieving 18 dB of squeezing and 20 dB of anti-squeezing at 1570 nm in a 1.6-cm traveling-wave adaptively poled thin-film lithium niobate waveguide. A distributed model independently determines facet losses, phase noise, and nonlinear interaction strength without prior assumptions, enabling rigorous inference of on-chip performance. We estimate a 95% confidence interval of [-18.96, -17.25] dB squeezing and [19.96, 21.35] dB anti-squeezing. These values represent the highest squeezing reported for any integrated photonic platform and the first assumption-free statistical validation of integrated squeezing performance. Our results establish thin-film lithium niobate as a high-performance, scalable platform for continuous-variable quantum sensing, communications, and photonic computing.
tldr: Demonstrates record 18 dB on-chip squeezing in an adaptively poled lithium niobate waveguide, enabling scalable continuous-variable quantum technologies.
motivation: To achieve high squeezing levels on a scalable integrated photonic platform for quantum sensing, communication, and computing.
method: Uses an adaptively poled thin-film lithium niobate waveguide with a distributed model to independently infer on-chip performance without prior assumptions.
result: Achieves 18 dB squeezing and 20 dB anti-squeezing at 1570 nm, with rigorous 95% confidence intervals, the highest squeezing reported for any integrated platform.
conclusion: Establishes thin-film lithium niobate as a high-performance scalable platform for continuous-variable quantum information processing, with implications for quantum communication and sensing.

title: Exciton-Tunable Phase Control And Superstrong Coupling Through Multimode Polariton Engineering In Planar Waveguides
authors: Johannes B\"urger, Erika Cortese, Simone Di Muzio, Daniele Sanvitto, Simone de Liberato, Dario Ballarini
abstract: ArXiv:2605.27714v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Strong light-matter coupling in optical waveguides provides a versatile platform for engineering hybrid polaritonic modes and their dispersion. Here we investigate multimode exciton-photon coupling in visible semiconductor waveguides supporting several transverse electric modes. Using rigorous coupled-wave analysis combined with a coupled-oscillator model, we show that the photonic band structure can be engineered across a range of regimes, from conventional multimode strong coupling to the superstrong coupling regime, where the Rabi splitting becomes comparable to the spacing between adjacent photonic modes. In the latter regime, hybridization between orthogonal electromagnetic modes is enabled by restricting the active material to a subregion of the mode volume where the photonic modes exhibit strong mutual overlap. This breaking of the orthogonality leads to polaritonic branches whose composition can be tuned among several photonic modes and the exciton. We demonstrate that small shifts of the exciton resonance produce pronounced changes in the propagation constants of different polariton branches, enabling exciton-controlled phase modulation through modal interference and, in the superstrong coupling regime, direct modal switching across a continuous S-shaped dispersion. The resulting figures of merit predict [MATH] phase shifts for exciton energy shifts of only a few meV over propagation lengths of tens of micrometers, while larger shifts are still required for mode switching. These results establish multimode waveguide polaritons as a versatile platform spanning multiple coupling regimes, for compact phase and intensity control in integrated photonic architectures.
tldr: This paper demonstrates multimode exciton-photon coupling in planar waveguides, achieving superstrong coupling and exciton-tunable phase control via modal interference.
motivation: To explore multimode polariton engineering in waveguides beyond the standard strong coupling regime, enabling compact phase and intensity control for integrated photonic circuits.
method: Rigorous coupled-wave analysis combined with a coupled-oscillator model to study multimode coupling between excitons and transverse electric modes in visible semiconductor waveguides.
result: Achieved superstrong coupling where Rabi splitting is comparable to photonic mode spacing, enabling exciton-controlled phase shifts of π over tens of micrometers and modal switching via continuous S-shaped dispersion.
conclusion: Multimode waveguide polaritons provide a versatile platform for compact phase and intensity control, with potential applications in integrated photonics and quantum information processing.

title: Memory-assisted Squeezed Light Velocimetry Under Realistic Loss And Incoherent Noise
authors: Mustafa G\"undo\u{g}an, Arash Ahmadi, Markus Krutzik
abstract: ArXiv:2605.27723v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a velocity sensor based on a two-memory Mach--Zehnder interferometer fed by a coherent probe and squeezed vacuum, read out by balanced homodyne detection. One memory is taken as a stationary reference, while the second memory moves during storage, so that its velocity is mapped onto a differential interferometric phase at readout. The two memories are otherwise assumed identical and are described by a Gaussian write--store--read lifetime together with the associated unconditional noise floor. Using the classical Fisher information, we derive the velocity sensitivity, the transmission threshold required for a target quantum gain, and the optimum storage time. The squeezed scheme improves on equal-resource coherent homodyne within an operating window set mainly by total transmission and phase stability. For representative near-term parameters, unconditional memory noise floors up to about [MATH] photons per trial do not by themselves remove the advantage; after optimization the improvement remains at the few-percent level and is limited chiefly by loss.
tldr: A velocity sensor using a two-memory Mach-Zehnder interferometer with squeezed light is analyzed under realistic loss and noise, showing quantum advantage persists for moderate memory noise.
motivation: To design a practical quantum-enhanced velocity sensor that can operate under realistic experimental imperfections such as loss and memory noise.
method: The authors model a Mach-Zehnder interferometer with two identical Gaussian memories (one moving), coherent probe and squeezed vacuum input, and balanced homodyne detection. They use classical Fisher information to derive sensitivity, transmission threshold, and optimal storage time.
result: The squeezed scheme outperforms coherent homodyne within an operating window set by total transmission and phase stability. Unconditional memory noise up to ~0.1 photons per trial does not eliminate the advantage, but improvement is limited to a few percent due to loss.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that quantum-enhanced velocimetry is feasible with near-term memory technology, but loss remains the primary limitation; future work could explore better squeezing or lower-loss memories.

title: Towards Entanglement-enhanced Probing Of Atomic Parity Violation
authors: Maxim Sirotin
abstract: ArXiv:2605.27775v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Atomic parity violation (APV) provides a low-energy probe of the weak interaction between electrons and nuclei, complementary to collider tests of the Standard Model. Isotope-chain measurements are especially attractive because they test weak-charge scaling while reducing dependence on absolute atomic-structure theory. We review the APV mechanism, the state of the art in Cs and Yb, and recent trapped-ion, optical-lattice, and molecular proposals. Motivated by progress in coherent control of atoms, ions, and molecules, we ask a metrological question: given N probes distributed over an isotope chain, what quantum strategy optimally measures a deviation from Standard Model weak-charge scaling? The optimum is a particular form of a cross-isotope cat state protocol. We compare this protocol with the standard quantum limit, squeezed-array, same-isotope cat, and discuss extension to recently suggested decoherence-free subspace protocols. We show that entanglement can strongly accelerate statistical averaging, but the ultimate precision is set by APV-specific systematic floors which require careful studies.
tldr: This paper proposes entanglement-enhanced quantum metrology protocols for measuring atomic parity violation across isotope chains, showing that cat states can accelerate statistical averaging but systematic floors limit ultimate precision.
motivation: Atomic parity violation (APV) offers a low-energy test of the Standard Model, and isotope-chain measurements reduce dependence on atomic theory. The goal is to find the optimal quantum strategy using N probes to detect deviations from Standard Model weak-charge scaling.
method: The authors review APV mechanisms and current experiments, then analyze quantum metrological protocols including cross-isotope cat states, squeezed arrays, same-isotope cat states, and decoherence-free subspace protocols, comparing their performance against the standard quantum limit.
result: The optimal protocol is a cross-isotope cat state that strongly accelerates statistical averaging. However, the ultimate precision is limited by APV-specific systematic errors, not quantum noise.
conclusion: Entanglement can significantly improve measurement speed, but careful systematic error analysis is needed. Future work should address these systematic floors to realize the full benefit of quantum enhancement.

title: Coherent Dark State Formation Of A Lead-Vacancy Spin Qubit In Diamond
authors: Yiyang Chen, Koyo Hirai, Tzyy Zheng Neo, Eiki Ota, Takashi Taniguchi, Masashi Miyakawa, Shinobu Onoda, Toshiharu Makino, Mutsuko Hatano, Takayuki Iwasaki
abstract: ArXiv:2605.27841v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A lead-vacancy (PbV) center in diamond exhibits coherent emission above the liquid helium temperature, making it highly attractive for quantum network applications. Here, we report the magneto-optical and spin properties of PbV centers in diamond. We record a spin lifetime of 12 ms at 7.5 K under large off-axis magnetic field. Furthermore, we observe formation of the coherent dark state by coherent population trapping and estimate a spin dephasing time of 354 ns at 6.5 K. This work demonstrates the outstanding thermal robustness of the PbV spin compared to other group-IV centers above 4 K.
tldr: This paper demonstrates coherent dark state formation and long spin lifetime in lead-vacancy centers in diamond, highlighting their potential for quantum network applications.
motivation: Group-IV color centers in diamond are promising for quantum networks, but most require cryogenic temperatures below 4 K. The PbV center shows coherent emission above liquid helium temperature, motivating investigation of its spin properties for practical quantum repeaters.
method: The authors performed magneto-optical spectroscopy and coherent population trapping experiments on PbV centers in diamond under off-axis magnetic fields at temperatures around 6.5-7.5 K.
result: They measured a spin lifetime of 12 ms at 7.5 K and observed coherent dark state formation via coherent population trapping, estimating a spin dephasing time of 354 ns at 6.5 K.
conclusion: The PbV center exhibits superior thermal robustness compared to other group-IV centers, making it a strong candidate for quantum network nodes operating above 4 K.

title: Entropic And Operational Characterizations Of Dynamic Quantum Resources
authors: Eric Chitambar Kaiyuan Ji
abstract: ArXiv:2112.06906v5 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We offer new methods for characterizing general closed and convex quantum resource theories, including dynamic ones, based on entropic concepts and operational tasks. We propose a resource-theoretic generalization of the quantum conditional min-entropy, termed the free conditional min-entropy (FCME), in the sense that it quantifies an observer's ``subjective'' degree of uncertainty about a quantum system given that the observer's information processing is limited to free operations of the resource theory. Using this generalized concept, we provide a complete set of entropic conditions for free convertibility between quantum states or channels in any closed and convex quantum resource theory. We also derive an information-theoretic interpretation for the resource global robustness of a state or a channel in terms of a mutual-information-like quantity based on the FCME. Apart from this entropic approach, we characterize dynamic resources by also analyzing their performance in operational tasks. We construct operationally meaningful and complete sets of resource monotones with these tasks, which enable faithful tests of free convertibility between quantum channels. Finally, we show that every well-defined robustness-based measure of a channel can be interpreted as an operational advantage of the channel over free channels in a communication task.
tldr: The paper develops entropic and operational characterizations for general quantum resource theories, including dynamic resources, with applications to convertibility and robustness measures.
motivation: To provide unified methods for quantifying and testing resource convertibility in quantum resource theories, especially for dynamic resources (channels), which are less studied than static resources.
method: Introduces the free conditional min-entropy (FCME) as a resource-theoretic generalization of conditional min-entropy, and constructs operational tasks that yield complete sets of resource monotones for channels.
result: Provides entropic conditions for free convertibility of states and channels, interprets global robustness as a mutual-information-like quantity, and shows that every robustness-based channel measure corresponds to an operational advantage in communication tasks.
conclusion: The framework offers powerful tools for analyzing dynamic quantum resources, with implications for quantum communication and information processing tasks.

title: Agreement And Compatibility In Wigner's Friend Paradox
authors: Julio C. F. Silva, B. F. Rizzuti, Cristhiano Duarte
abstract: ArXiv:2605.27424v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: There has been an upsurge of interest in the consequences for quantum physics of the so-called Wigner's Friend Paradox. In its original formulation, the paradox has been turned inside out, and virtually every aspect of it has been looked into. Consequently, it is becoming widely accepted that we can find the potentially puzzling consequences of Wigner's thought experiment only in light of its many-parties extensions. Nonetheless, this contribution returns to the source. Reframing the question as an inference problem, we advance a radically Bayesian interpretation that shows no contradiction between Wigner's and Wigner's Friend's descriptions-neither classically nor quantumly. Therefore, with no paradoxical conclusion. In doing so, we flesh out and expose previously untouched aspects of Winger's thought experiment, in particular, the fact that compatibility and agreement are fundamental to our understanding of it. Also, by conservatively extending Wigner's original setup and incorporating what we call the 'benefit of the doubt', we see how either Wigner's or his Friend's description can be driven to match one another's -- an impossibility if either agent does not keep an open mind.
tldr: The paper resolves Wigner's Friend paradox using a Bayesian interpretation, showing no contradiction between agents' descriptions.
motivation: To address the long-standing Wigner's Friend paradox and its implications for quantum foundations, particularly the consistency of quantum descriptions among different observers.
method: The authors reframe the paradox as an inference problem and adopt a radically Bayesian interpretation, introducing concepts of compatibility, agreement, and 'benefit of the doubt' to reconcile Wigner's and his friend's descriptions.
result: They demonstrate that there is no contradiction between the two descriptions, either classically or quantumly, and show how each agent's description can be driven to match the other's if they keep an open mind.
conclusion: The paradox is resolved without requiring modifications to quantum mechanics, highlighting the importance of Bayesian reasoning and open-mindedness in quantum inference.

title: Quantum Reservoir Networks Based On Decoherence-free Subspaces
authors: V. V. Akshay, M. V. Altaisky, N. E. Kaputkina
abstract: ArXiv:2605.27427v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present numerical simulation of a six-qubit quantum reservoir network with an output implemented on a 5-dimensional decoherence-free subspace (DFS), working as a classifier between entangled and product states of the input quantum system, fed to the reservoir during a finite learning time. Since the dynamics of DFS is not affected by external fluctuations, no cooling is required, and the proposed model seems a promising candidate for future quantum artificial intelligence systems working at room temperatures and free of huge energy consumption.
tldr: A six-qubit quantum reservoir network using a decoherence-free subspace is simulated to classify entangled vs. product states without cooling, promising room-temperature quantum AI.
motivation: To demonstrate a quantum reservoir network that operates without cooling by leveraging decoherence-free subspaces, reducing energy consumption and enabling room-temperature quantum machine learning.
method: Numerical simulation of a six-qubit quantum reservoir network with a 5-dimensional decoherence-free subspace as output, trained to classify input quantum states as entangled or product.
result: The DFS-based reservoir successfully classifies entangled and product states after finite learning time, with dynamics unaffected by external fluctuations.
conclusion: The model suggests a path toward energy-efficient, room-temperature quantum AI systems, though experimental realization and scalability remain to be addressed.

title: Lowering Lcu Circuit Width Through Maximum-Weight Birkhoff-von Neumann Decomposition
authors: Ammar Daskin
abstract: ArXiv:2605.27430v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Any square matrix can be transformed into a doubly stochastic matrix via Sinkhorn scaling with diagonal matrices or completing to a larger dimensional matrix. Standard Birkhoff-von Neumann and Pauli decompositions represent such matrices as linear combinations of [MATH] permutation or Pauli terms, leading to a large ancilla overhead in a quantum Linear Combination of Unitaries (LCU) implementation. We prove that a bottleneck variant of Birkhoff's algorithm reduces the number of permutations to [MATH], where [MATH] is the [MATH]-norm approximation error of the reconstructed matrix, and demonstrate empirically that a largest-weight greedy variant requires only [MATH] terms for dense matrices (the exact average observed is [MATH]). The quadratic reduction in term count directly shrinks the ancilla register from [MATH] to [MATH] qubits, shortens the SELECT circuit, and is especially valuable in fixed-Hadamard LCU architectures whose success probability scales with [MATH]. The approach enables compact quantum implementations of dense operators appearing in optimal transport, non-Hermitian simulation, and other settings amenable to Sinkhorn preconditioning. Furthermore, because the decomposition is a convex combination, the LCU normalization constant is exactly [MATH], and the uniform superposition is an eigenvector of the target matrix with eigenvalue~1. This structure can be exploited to achieve high success probability without amplitude amplification in many practical scenarios, including quantum walks and Markov chain simulations.
tldr: This paper reduces the ancilla qubit count in LCU circuits by using a maximum-weight Birkhoff-von Neumann decomposition, achieving quadratic reduction in permutation terms.
motivation: Standard LCU implementations require many ancilla qubits due to the number of permutation terms in the Birkhoff decomposition, limiting practical quantum circuits. The authors aim to reduce this overhead.
method: They prove a bottleneck variant of Birkhoff's algorithm reduces permutations to O(1/ε^2) and empirically show a greedy largest-weight variant requires only O(N) terms for dense matrices, compared to O(N^2) standard.
result: The ancilla register shrinks from O(log N^2) to O(log N) qubits, and the SELECT circuit is shortened. The LCU normalization constant is exactly 1, enabling high success probability without amplitude amplification in many cases.
conclusion: This approach enables compact quantum implementations of dense operators, benefiting applications like optimal transport and non-Hermitian simulation, and can be exploited in quantum walks and Markov chain simulations.

title: Raman Spectroscopy At Metal Interfaces: A Numerical Study Of The Strong Coupling Regime
authors: Zeyu Zhou, Maxim Sukharev, Abraham Nitzan, Joseph Eli Subotnik
abstract: ArXiv:2605.27609v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate how proximity to a metal nanostructure, particularly to a flat mirror or a cavity confined between two mirrors, affects the vibronic structure of Raman scattering signals. We find that such proximity, particularly for the strong-coupling situation encountered in cavity environments, plays multiple roles in shaping Raman signals beyond the now-familiar signal enhancement known as surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS). First, in analogy to the electromagnetic SERS mechanism, near or between mirrors, the local field experienced by a molecule differ from that in vacuum. In particular, between mirrors, the cavity enhances the effective excited state population by trapping the EM field inside it. Second, the nearby metal surface provides a relaxation channel and a lineshape broadening mechanism, and inside a cavity this lineshape is inherited by the cavity polaritons. This relaxation results in a loss of yield but the associated broadening also leads to significant absorption over a larger frequency range. Third, near metallic interfaces interference between incident and reflected light can lead to a richly structured Raman spectrum. For instance, we find that the Rabi contraction (that results from depopulating the ground state) can interfere with Raman signals (and the effect appears to be the same order as Raman itself). These cavity effects are calculated by a full-scale FDTD simulation and highlight the convoluted but fascinating roles of photonic materials on optical signals.
tldr: This paper numerically studies how metal interfaces and cavities modify Raman scattering signals, including strong coupling effects and Rabi contraction.
motivation: To understand the multiple roles of metal proximity and cavity confinement on Raman signals beyond standard SERS enhancement.
method: Full-scale finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations of a molecule near a flat mirror or between two mirrors.
result: Cavity enhances effective excited state population, metal provides relaxation and broadening, and interference between incident and reflected light yields structured spectra; Rabi contraction interferes with Raman signals.
conclusion: Photonic materials have convoluted effects on optical signals, with implications for designing hybrid quantum systems and understanding strong coupling.

title: Full Characterization Of Informative Subsets In Quantum Encrypted Cloning
authors: Gabriele Gianini, Stelvio Cimato, Jianyi Lin, Omar Hasan, Ernesto Damiani
abstract: ArXiv:2605.27421v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum encrypted cloning, introduced by Yamaguchi and Kempf, is a Pauli-based protocol that distributes an unknown input qubit into multiple encrypted signal-noise pairs in such a way that redundancy is created without violating the no-cloning theorem, since at most one clone can later be perfectly recovered through an appropriate decoding procedure. In previous work we showed that unauthorized subsets of the storage register are not, in general, completely uninformative, and we identified a parity-dependent leakage pattern. In the present work we extend the analysis to subsets that also include the transformed source qubit A. Exploiting the purity of the global encoded state and the complementarity between storage-only subsets and subsets containing A, we derive a full classification of the informativeness of all sets of the form [MATH]. We show that these subsets are fully informative in the generic case. Two exceptions arise. First, if all pairs are incomplete and |C|<n, then the reduced state is completely uninformative. Second, if |C|=n, n is odd, and the number q of signal qubits in C is even, then the reduced state is partially informative. In this latter case, the residual dependence on the input state is confined to the y-component of the Bloch vector. These results provide a complete parity-based characterization of leakage for subsets containing the transformed input qubit.
tldr: This paper fully characterizes the informativeness of subsets containing the transformed input qubit in quantum encrypted cloning, revealing a parity-based leakage pattern.
motivation: Previous work identified partial information leakage in storage-only subsets; this work extends the analysis to subsets including the transformed source qubit to complete the classification.
method: The authors exploit the purity of the global encoded state and complementarity between storage-only subsets and subsets containing A, deriving a full classification of informativeness for all subsets of the form [MATH].
result: Subsets are fully informative in the generic case, except when all pairs are incomplete and |C|<n (completely uninformative) or when |C|=n, n odd, and the number of signal qubits in C is even (partially informative, with residual dependence on the y-component of the Bloch vector).
conclusion: The results provide a complete parity-based characterization of information leakage for subsets containing the transformed input qubit, which is important for understanding security in quantum encrypted cloning protocols.

title: Competition For Survival And The Maximum Entropy Production Principle In Self-Organized Silver Particle Chains
authors: Albert Han, Jiri Kataman-Kustwan, Alexey Bezryadin
abstract: ArXiv:2605.27457v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The maximum entropy production (MEP) principle is a hypothetical law of physics which dictates that complex systems, far from equilibrium, evolve into an ordered dissipative structure (DS) which generates as much entropy per second as possible. An important problem is whether the natural competition for resources, limits the ability of DS to achieve the maximum of the entropy production rate (EPR). We investigate this competition between DS by performing high precision electrical measurements on suspensions of silver particles under electric fields. To establish the impact of competition on MEP principle, precise electrical measurements are performed on two Ag suspension samples connected in parallel. The samples are able to self-organize, dissipate energy, generate entropy, and compete with each other for resources, i.e., electrical current. Our findings are as follows: (1) There is a competition between the two samples, which prevents both systems from achieving their maximum possible contribution to the global entropy production rate. (2) Due to this competition, we find that only one out of two samples can self-organize, while the other deteriorates and approaches zero EPR. (3) The global EPR, i.e., the entropy produced by the samples and the energy supply circuit, is also reduced from its possible maximum due to the competition between the sub-systems. Based on these observations, we propose that the competition effect constitutes an essential constraint that must be incorporated into formulations of the MEP. This principle parallels real-world phenomena, reflecting the competition for resources observed among species and individual organisms in natural systems. We also examine the global implications of the MEP and propose that it serves as a driving mechanism propelling the hypothetical ascent of civilizations along the Kardashev scale.
tldr: This paper experimentally tests the maximum entropy production principle in competing self-organized silver particle chains, finding that competition reduces global entropy production.
motivation: To investigate whether competition for resources limits the ability of dissipative structures to achieve maximum entropy production rate, a key open question in nonequilibrium thermodynamics.
method: High-precision electrical measurements on two parallel silver suspension samples under electric fields, allowing self-organization and competition for current.
result: Competition prevents both samples from achieving maximum EPR; only one self-organizes while the other deteriorates; global EPR is reduced from its possible maximum.
conclusion: Competition is an essential constraint for MEP principle, with implications for understanding dissipative structures and even societal evolution (Kardashev scale).

title: Displaced Gaussian Boson Sampling For Enhanced Max-clique Search
authors: Ewan Mer, Zhenghao Li, Shang Yu, Ian A. Walmsley, Raj B. Patel
abstract: ArXiv:2605.27522v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gaussian Boson Sampling (GBS) is capable of solving certain classes of graph problems owing to the samples produced by such a device having a connection to the hafnian matrix function. In particular, a GBS device has been shown to provide an enhancement in the search of cliques -- or complete subgraphs -- in undirected weighted graphs over classical algorithms. A graph can be mapped to a GBS experiment by configuring the squeezing parameters of the input states and programming the linear optical network. In practice, limited squeezing and photon loss degrade the performance of the GBS device for max-clique search. In comparison, coherent states -- often considered a classical resource due to their Poissonian statistics -- can be readily prepared across many modes using an attenuated laser. In this paper, we report an enhancement of the success rate of GBS in finding maximum weighted cliques by adding displacements under lossy conditions or when a limited amount of squeezing is available. Moreover, we report that this enhancement can be scaled up to large graphs with limited resource overheads.
tldr: Adding displacements to Gaussian Boson Sampling improves max-clique search under lossy or limited-squeezing conditions.
motivation: GBS can solve graph problems like max-clique search but suffers from photon loss and limited squeezing in practice. Coherent states are easier to prepare, so the authors investigate whether adding displacements can enhance performance.
method: The authors theoretically and numerically analyze GBS with displaced squeezed states, comparing success probabilities for finding maximum weighted cliques under various loss and squeezing levels.
result: Displacements significantly boost the success rate of GBS for max-clique search when squeezing is low or loss is high, and the enhancement scales to large graphs with modest resource overhead.
conclusion: Displaced GBS offers a practical improvement for quantum-enhanced graph algorithms, potentially making GBS more robust for near-term quantum devices.

title: Three-fold Coincidence By Stimulated Parametric Down-conversion
authors: Yishai Klein, Alessio D'errico, Farid Ghobadi, Dilip Paneru, Nazanin Dehghan, Eliahu Cohen, Ebrahim Karimi
abstract: ArXiv:2605.27653v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Parametric down-conversion is a widely used source of nonclassical light in quantum optics and photonic quantum technologies. While stimulated parametric down-conversion with strong classical seeds is well studied, the regime in which stimulation occurs at the single-photon level has hitherto remained largely unexplored experimentally. Here, we study continuous-wave, low-gain down-conversion seeded by a weak coherent field with an average photon number well below one per coherence time. By measuring third-order temporal correlations, we observe a clear enhancement that cannot be accounted for by spontaneous processes or accidental coincidences alone, and is consistent with stimulation involving the seed and the generated photon pair. These results provide time-domain evidence of seed-induced three-photon correlations and suggest new ways to engineer and probe multi-photon states for quantum imaging, sensing, and information processing.
tldr: This paper experimentally demonstrates three-fold coincidence enhancement in stimulated parametric down-conversion at the single-photon level, providing time-domain evidence of seed-induced three-photon correlations.
motivation: Stimulated parametric down-conversion with weak seeds (single-photon level) has been largely unexplored experimentally, yet it could enable new ways to engineer multi-photon states for quantum technologies.
method: Continuous-wave, low-gain parametric down-conversion seeded by a weak coherent field (average photon number <1 per coherence time) was used, and third-order temporal correlations were measured.
result: A clear enhancement in three-fold coincidences was observed that cannot be explained by spontaneous processes or accidental coincidences, consistent with stimulation involving the seed and the generated photon pair.
conclusion: The results provide time-domain evidence of seed-induced three-photon correlations and suggest new approaches for quantum imaging, sensing, and information processing.

title: Radiative Response Of Atomic Systems Illuminated With Approximate Spherical Vector Waves
authors: R. J\'auregui F. Camas-Aquino
abstract: ArXiv:2605.27558v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The natural electromagnetic modes spontaneously emitted by an atom in free space are spherical vector waves (SVWs). Each SVW mode is uniquely linked to a specific dynamical--spherical--multipole--moment of the atomic system. In this work, we introduce a general formalism for evaluating spherical multipole transition rates under different boundary conditions, considering the superposition between a given SVW and the modes resulting from the boundary conditions. This formalism is applied to study the radiative properties of an atomic system trapped near the focus of a 4[MATH] optical array. By appropriately selecting the external light field, the juxtaposed lenses of the optical array allow the atom to be illuminated with approximate spherical vector waves. Explicit expressions for the resulting multipole transition rates are presented as a function of the numerical aperture of the lenses. The feasibility of enhancing and inhibiting electric dipole-forbidden transitions using such an array, under current experimental capabilities, is briefly discussed.
tldr: This paper develops a formalism for calculating spherical multipole transition rates of atoms illuminated by approximate spherical vector waves, with application to an atom near the focus of a 4π optical array.
motivation: To understand and control radiative properties of atomic systems under realistic boundary conditions, particularly for enhancing or inhibiting electric dipole-forbidden transitions.
method: The authors introduce a general formalism that evaluates spherical multipole transition rates by considering the superposition of a given spherical vector wave (SVW) with modes resulting from boundary conditions. They apply this to an atom trapped near the focus of a 4π optical array, deriving explicit expressions as a function of numerical aperture.
result: Explicit expressions for multipole transition rates are presented, and the feasibility of enhancing/inhibiting electric dipole-forbidden transitions using the optical array is discussed.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for controlling atomic radiative properties via tailored light fields, with potential applications in quantum optics and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Efficient Ensemble Randomization By Tuning Chaos In A Nonlinear Spin-1 System
authors: Jongmin Kim, Minsung Jeong, Jongyoon Han, Y. Shin
abstract: ArXiv:2605.27448v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an efficient scheme to randomize a spin-state ensemble in a nonlinear spin-1 system by tuning chaos with an external periodic drive. Without modulation, the system exhibits a mixed phase space featuring regular islands embedded in a chaotic sea, where global mixing is inhibited by energy conservation. Using numerical simulations, we demonstrate that weak modulation of a linear Zeeman field not only facilitates transport between different energy shells but also drives ensembles toward a Haar-random distribution over spin states. Under optimized conditions, complete randomization is achieved on a timescale set by the inverse nonlinear interaction energy. In the overdriven regime, randomization is unexpectedly suppressed at specific modulation amplitudes, accompanied by the formation of sticky regions in phase space. We attribute this behavior to the dynamical cancellation of the leading low-order harmonic component of the periodic drive. These results illustrate how time-periodic driving can be used to engineer chaotic systems and achieve controllable randomization in nonlinear spin systems.
tldr: This paper demonstrates efficient randomization of a spin-1 ensemble by tuning chaos with a periodic drive, achieving Haar-random distribution on timescales set by inverse nonlinear interaction energy.
motivation: To develop a fast and controllable method for randomizing spin ensembles, which is important for quantum information processing and metrology.
method: Numerical simulations of a nonlinear spin-1 system under weak modulation of a linear Zeeman field, analyzing phase space transport and randomization efficiency.
result: Weak modulation enables transport between energy shells and drives the ensemble to Haar-random distribution; overdriving suppresses randomization due to dynamical cancellation of low-order harmonics.
conclusion: Time-periodic driving can engineer chaos for controllable randomization in nonlinear spin systems, with potential applications in quantum state preparation.

title: Sympathetic Cooling In Trapped Ions With Spectral Selectivity Via The Zeeman Shift
authors: Kavyashree Ranawat, Jiyong Yu, Andrew van Horn, Jacob Whitlow, Kenneth R Brown, Jungsang Kim
abstract: ArXiv:2605.27577v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-fidelity quantum logic operations in trapped ions often require the ions' collective motion to be cooled to near the ground state. Since cooling the ions' motion typically involves dissipative processes such as spontaneous photon scattering, sympathetic cooling is used on select coolant ions between gate sequences to cool the ion chain without affecting the data qubits. Common implementations for coolant ions include different atomic species, different isotopes of the same species or individually addressable ions. Each of these approaches have challenges associated with them, which include increased hardware complexity, reduced efficiency of radial mode cooling and re-ordering events which add additional experimental overhead. We demonstrate a sympathetic cooling scheme leveraging internal metastable atomic levels accessible via a narrow quadrupole transition, utilizing the natural Zeeman shift and individually addressed Raman transitions, to achieve isolation of the non-coolant or ``data ions" from coolant ions. We demonstrate modest decoherence of the data ions due to cooling, while preserving the coherence requirements for high-fidelity gate operations.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a sympathetic cooling scheme for trapped ions using Zeeman-shift-based spectral selectivity to isolate data ions from coolant ions, reducing decoherence.
motivation: To overcome challenges in sympathetic cooling of trapped ions, such as hardware complexity and reduced cooling efficiency, by using internal metastable states and Zeeman shifts.
method: The scheme uses a narrow quadrupole transition to access metastable atomic levels, combined with Zeeman shifts and individually addressed Raman transitions to selectively cool coolant ions without affecting data ions.
result: The method achieves modest decoherence of data ions during cooling, preserving coherence for high-fidelity gate operations.
conclusion: The approach offers a simpler alternative to multi-species or isotope-based sympathetic cooling, with potential for improved scalability in trapped-ion quantum computing.

title: Geometric Analysis Of Variational Quantum Eigensolver
authors: Zhen Qin
abstract: ArXiv:2605.27795v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) is a fundamental algorithm in quantum computing, yet a coherent geometric characterization of VQE remains missing due to fragmented analyses across fixed-ansatz and adaptive-circuit formulations. In this paper, we establish a geometric analysis of VQE in terms of optimization landscape, initialization guarantee, and noise robustness. First, we study the optimization landscape via an ansatz-free product-unitary formulation over the unitary group, unifying both paradigms. For the single-unitary case, we establish linear convergence of Riemannian gradient descent (RGD) and prove the strict saddle property. For the product-unitary case, we show the convergence rate deteriorates polynomially with circuit depth, providing a geometric explanation of the barren plateau phenomenon. Second, we prove that small-angle random Pauli-rotation circuits satisfy the required initialization conditions with high probability. Third, we show that RGD retains linear convergence under finite-shot measurements, and that coefficient-adaptive allocation achieves strictly lower statistical error than uniform sampling under a fixed measurement budget.
tldr: This paper provides a geometric analysis of the Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE), focusing on optimization landscapes, initialization guarantees, and noise robustness.
motivation: VQE is a key quantum algorithm but lacks a unified geometric characterization across different formulations.
method: The authors use an ansatz-free product-unitary formulation over the unitary group and analyze Riemannian gradient descent (RGD) convergence.
result: They prove linear convergence for single-unitary VQE, show polynomial deterioration with circuit depth, and demonstrate that small-angle random Pauli-rotation circuits satisfy initialization conditions with high probability.
conclusion: The geometric perspective explains barren plateaus and provides insights for efficient measurement allocation under noise.

title: Blind Prng Hijacking: An Undetectable Integrity-Preserving Attack Against Llm Watermarking
authors: Ziyang You, Huilong He, Xiaoke Yang, Xuxing Lu
abstract: ArXiv:2605.28632v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cryptographic watermarking is a leading defense for attributing text generated by large language models (LLMs). Existing schemes, including KGW, Unigram, and DipMark, derive their security guarantees from the assumption that the underlying pseudo-random number generator (PRNG) is trustworthy. This work introduces SeedHijack, the first supply-chain attack on LLM watermarking that is simultaneously (i) blind -- requiring no knowledge of the watermark key, detector, or model logits, (ii) integrity-preserving -- amplifying rather than erasing the watermark signal, and (iii) orthogonal to detection -- the attack-induced bias is statistically independent of all content-side detector statistics, ensuring that amplification and evasion coexist without trade-off. Rather than perturbing generated text, SeedHijack replaces the PRNG at the supply-chain layer, biasing green-list selection without altering output tokens or degrading text quality. Across three watermarking schemes and three open-source LLMs, the attack triggers 0/6 state-of-the-art content-side statistical detectors while inflating the watermark z-score up to 2.42x (system-level defenses such as entropy-source attestation remain orthogonal and complementary). A quantum random number generator (QRNG) countermeasure is shown to fully neutralize the attack while preserving benign watermarking utility. These findings establish PRNG integrity as a first-class security requirement for cryptographic content-provenance systems.
tldr: This paper introduces a supply-chain attack on LLM watermarking by hijacking the PRNG, and proposes a QRNG countermeasure.
motivation: To expose a vulnerability in cryptographic watermarking for LLMs that assumes PRNG trustworthiness, and to demonstrate an attack that is blind, integrity-preserving, and orthogonal to detection.
method: The attack replaces the PRNG at the supply-chain layer to bias green-list selection without altering output tokens; a QRNG-based countermeasure is proposed and tested.
result: The attack evades six state-of-the-art detectors while inflating watermark z-scores up to 2.42x; QRNG fully neutralizes the attack.
conclusion: PRNG integrity is a critical security requirement for content-provenance systems; QRNG offers a viable countermeasure.

title: Photon-Conditioned Squeezed States For Directional Displacement Response In Continuous-Variable Photonics
authors: Olivier Pfister Boris Kiefer
abstract: ArXiv:2605.27660v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Squeezed Fock states, photon-subtracted squeezed states, and optical cat states are established non-Gaussian resources in continuous-variable quantum optics. Here we compare these known state families from a task-oriented perspective: matched mean photon number, scalar Wigner negativity, and directional displacement-fidelity response. Starting from squeezed vacuum, single-photon subtraction prepares a state proportional to \(S(r,\theta)\), while two-photon subtraction prepares an even-parity squeezed Fock superposition rather than a pure \(S(r,\theta)\). We benchmark photon-conditioned squeezed states against Fock and coherent-cat references using the integrated Wigner negativity \(\delta\), the energy-normalized metric \(\delta/\langle n\rangle\), and fidelity-threshold displacement radii \(R_F(\phi)\). Cat benchmarks remain strong scalar Wigner-negativity resources, whereas photon-conditioned squeezed states provide an origin-centered alternative with tunable anisotropic displacement response. In particular, the two-photon-subtracted squeezed state shows favorable displacement-fidelity radii over selected quadrature directions at matched \(\langle n\rangle\). These results identify a regime relevant to homodyne-aligned continuous-variable control and anisotropic displacement-noise mitigation, with directional sensing as a natural dual application.
tldr: This paper compares photon-conditioned squeezed states with other non-Gaussian states for directional displacement response, focusing on Wigner negativity and fidelity thresholds.
motivation: To identify which non-Gaussian continuous-variable states offer the best performance for tasks like directional sensing and noise mitigation.
method: The authors compare squeezed Fock states, photon-subtracted squeezed states, and cat states using metrics like integrated Wigner negativity, energy-normalized negativity, and fidelity-threshold displacement radii.
result: Cat states have the highest scalar Wigner negativity, but two-photon-subtracted squeezed states provide tunable anisotropic displacement response with favorable fidelity radii in certain quadrature directions.
conclusion: Photon-conditioned squeezed states are promising for homodyne-aligned control and directional displacement-noise mitigation, with potential applications in sensing.

title: Neural Quantum Spectral Operator Learning For Solving Partial Differential Equations
authors: Chanyoung Kim, Myeonghwan Seong, Yujin Kim, Daniel K. Park, Youngjoon Hong
abstract: ArXiv:2605.27408v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Partial differential equations (PDEs) are central to modeling physical and engineering systems, but repeatedly solving parametric PDEs remains computationally expensive. Operator learning enables fast surrogate inference, yet typically requires large input-output paired datasets generated by costly high-fidelity PDE solvers. Unsupervised operator learning frameworks alleviate data dependency but remain hindered by computational bottlenecks. To address this, we propose Neural Variational Quantum Linear Solver (NVQLS), the first hybrid quantum-classical operator learning framework leveraging the Legendre--Galerkin weak formulation. We critically resolve the sign ambiguity in VQLS energy minimization, preventing erroneous solution representations. Additionally, we introduce a neural embedding, a novel encoding scheme to map varying forcings and PDE coefficients into parameterized quantum circuit representations. These structural innovations provide theoretical computational complexity advantages under efficient state preparation schemes, while achieving superior accuracy compared to a representative classical baseline. Validations on 1D and 2D parametric PDEs under diverse boundary conditions demonstrate NVQLS's capability to simultaneously process varying inputs, offering a scalable unsupervised approach to quantum-enhanced operator learning.
tldr: This paper proposes a hybrid quantum-classical operator learning framework for solving parametric PDEs using variational quantum linear solvers and Legendre-Galerkin methods.
motivation: Solving parametric PDEs repeatedly is computationally expensive; existing operator learning methods require large datasets or suffer from computational bottlenecks.
method: The authors introduce Neural Variational Quantum Linear Solver (NVQLS), which combines a variational quantum linear solver with Legendre-Galerkin weak formulation and a neural embedding to encode varying PDE parameters into quantum circuits.
result: NVQLS resolves sign ambiguity in VQLS energy minimization, provides theoretical computational complexity advantages, and achieves superior accuracy compared to a classical baseline on 1D and 2D parametric PDEs.
conclusion: The framework offers a scalable unsupervised approach to quantum-enhanced operator learning, with potential for broader applications in scientific computing.

title: Zero-shot Quantum Neural Architecture Search
authors: Tung Dao, Son Tran, Huynh Thi Thanh Binh
abstract: ArXiv:2605.27410v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Variational Quantum Algorithms (VQAs) are a leading approach to exploiting near-term quantum hardware, leveraging parameterized quantum circuits and classical optimization to achieve advantage. Despite their promise, the practical deployment of VQAs is challenged by the difficulty of designing quantum circuit architectures that balance expressivity, trainability, and hardware constraints. Existing evolutionary-based quantum neural architecture search methods address these challenges but suffer from high computational costs due to repeated training of candidate circuits. In this work, we identify a setting in which the Gram matrix of the Quantum Neural Tangent Kernel converges. Building on this observation, we design a zero-shot surrogate model to estimate candidate performance without full training, significantly accelerating the architecture search process. Using this surrogate, we propose MZeQAS, a Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS)-based Zero-Shot Quantum Neural Architecture Search framework for VQAs. By integrating proxy-based performance estimation with MCTS exploration, MZeQAS efficiently discovers high-performing architectures. Experimental results demonstrate that MZeQAS outperforms existing approaches in terms of both search efficiency and solution quality, providing a scalable and effective framework for advancing VQA deployment on noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices.
tldr: This paper proposes a zero-shot quantum neural architecture search method using Monte Carlo Tree Search and a surrogate model based on the Quantum Neural Tangent Kernel to accelerate variational quantum algorithm design.
motivation: Existing evolutionary-based quantum architecture search methods are computationally expensive due to repeated training of candidate circuits.
method: The authors identify a setting where the Gram matrix of the Quantum Neural Tangent Kernel converges, enabling a zero-shot surrogate model to estimate candidate performance without full training. They integrate this surrogate with Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) to form MZeQAS.
result: MZeQAS outperforms existing approaches in search efficiency and solution quality on benchmark tasks.
conclusion: The framework provides a scalable and effective way to deploy VQAs on NISQ devices, but the paper focuses on algorithm design rather than fundamental physics or quantum communication.

title: Can Quantum Federated Learning Withstand Circuit-Level Backdoors?
authors: Aakar Mathur, Mohammed Ruknuddin, Ashish Gupta
abstract: ArXiv:2605.27416v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum Federated Learning (QFL) inherits the core vulnerability of federated optimization to malicious clients, while also introducing an attack surface from variational circuit training and measurement-driven gradients. This work proposes a novel CircUit-Level backdoor Threat (CULT) model that formalizes four stealthy attacks by exploiting quantum-aware mechanisms, including Grover, Pauli, Bit-flip, and Sign-flip. By enabling malicious clients on both in-training and post-training surfaces, these attacks can critically undermine the learning process. We establish a rigorous theoretical foundation to demonstrate attack stealthiness under standard smoothness assumptions. Experiments on the MNIST and CIFAR-10 datasets with non-IID splits and varying fractions of malicious clients show that even a single malicious client can induce severe accuracy degradation under FedAvg aggregation. While popular defenses, including Krum, Multi-Krum, FoolsGold, FLGuardian, and Mud-HoG, reduce degradation in many regimes, they fail to eliminate worst-case failure cases, where accuracy drops up to 50\%. The experimental analysis further reveals that under the CULT model, malicious updates effectively mask their presence by staying close to benign norms, thereby helping attackers evade detection.
tldr: This paper proposes a circuit-level backdoor threat model for quantum federated learning and evaluates its impact on accuracy under various defenses.
motivation: Quantum federated learning inherits vulnerabilities from classical federated learning and introduces new attack surfaces from variational circuits; the authors aim to formalize and demonstrate these threats.
method: The authors define four stealthy attacks (Grover, Pauli, Bit-flip, Sign-flip) exploiting quantum mechanisms, and test them on MNIST and CIFAR-10 with non-IID splits and FedAvg aggregation, evaluating several classical defenses.
result: Even a single malicious client can cause severe accuracy degradation (up to 50% drop), and existing defenses fail to eliminate worst-case failures; malicious updates stay close to benign norms to evade detection.
conclusion: Quantum federated learning is vulnerable to circuit-level backdoors, and new quantum-aware defenses are needed.

title: Quantum Machine Learning-based 6g Edge Network: Enabling Adaptive Communication And Model Aggregation
authors: Wenjing Xiao, Jiatai Yan, Chenglong Shi, Shixin Chen, Miaojiang Chen, Min Chen, Saif Al-Kuwari, Ahmed Farouk
abstract: ArXiv:2605.27417v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: With the advent of sixth-generation (6G) mobile communication technology, vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication faces unprecedented challenges in communication efficiency, system generalization capabilities, and model collaboration. Conventional machine learning struggles with high-dimensional state spaces, slow convergence, and poor generalization under heterogeneous V2X nodes, rapidly varying channels, and multimodal sensing data in V2X systems.
